target.title: feat(slack): open group DMs from App Home
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack does not let people add an app to an existing people-only group DM, and OpenClaw did not provide a supported way to create the equivalent bot-inclusive conversation. Searching for the app in Slack's **Add people** dialog therefore returns no result, while `/openclaw` starts a session without changing the conversation membership.

Fixes #102038.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an inline App Home flow instead of another slash command or modal:

- a native Slack people picker selects 1–7 other members;
- the authenticated actor and OpenClaw are included automatically;
- `conversations.open` creates or resumes the exact-member MPIM;
- the existing catch-all block-action listener owns the click, preserving one acknowledgement and preventing an agent wake-up;
- existing DM authorization and group-DM configuration remain the gate;
- the generated Socket Mode manifest now enables interactivity.

The Slack guide explains setup, authorization, exact-member resumption, relay limitations, troubleshooting, and the key platform constraint: this creates a separate bot-inclusive group DM and cannot copy history from the original people-only DM. Users who need to preserve that history can instead convert the original group DM to a private channel and invite OpenClaw there.

## User Impact

When Slack DMs and unrestricted group DMs are enabled, an authorized user can open **Apps → OpenClaw → Home**, choose people, and open the resulting group DM. Everyone selected can use the agent in that conversation, which is disclosed in the picker and documentation. Existing configurations with group DMs disabled or concrete-only group-DM allowlists do not expose the control.

Related documentation work in #101944 by @clawSean covers general group-DM membership semantics; this PR preserves that scope and adds only the implemented App Home creation flow.

Release-note context: Slack users can create or resume bot-inclusive group DMs from OpenClaw's App Home.

## Evidence

- AWS Crabbox run `run_fec2cfe63716`: 73 focused Slack tests passed across App Home, block-action routing, and setup-manifest coverage before the final authorization hardening.
- AWS Crabbox run `run_177b3c67449e`: changed-file gates passed, including extension production/test `tsgo`, lint, plugin SDK boundaries, conflict/dependency/runtime guards, and import-cycle checks.
- Documentation checks passed directly: 701 MDX files, i18n glossary, 5,758 internal links with 0 broken links, generated docs map current, and `git diff --check` clean.
- Manual review covered the App Home ownership seam, Bolt listener overlap, authorization/delegation semantics, Slack API limits, exact-member reopening, and documentation accuracy.
- Fresh autoreview found an unpaired-creator authorization bypass; the flow now reuses `authorizeSlackDirectMessage`, includes pairing-store approvals, displays pairing instructions privately in App Home, and has a regression test. The required rerun completed with zero findings.

Known proof gaps:

- A live Slack create/reopen round trip was not run because no workspace credential was authorized for this task. The Slack Web API contract and installed SDK types were inspected directly; CI and reviewer live verification remain useful because Slack's scope documentation is internally inconsistent about bot-token MPIM creation.
- The post-hardening focused test rerun could not start because the reusable AWS lease was no longer available and the disposable dependency tree had been pruned. Draft CI run `28922743345` admitted the exact SHA but intentionally skipped test jobs; exact-head test proof remains for the ready-for-review run.
- The aggregate `check:docs`/anchor wrappers could not finish after `pnpm dlx` corrupted its disposable cache (`ERR_PNPM_NO_IMPORTER_MANIFEST_FOUND`); their component MDX, glossary, link, and docs-map checks passed as listed above.

target.title: fix(ssrf): allow loopback for hostnames in allowedHostnames list (#101965)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SSRF loopback tightening in #100835 blocked loopback addresses for all trusted hostnames, including those explicitly listed in the browser navigation guard's `allowedHostnames`. This broke the contract that explicitly allowed hostnames should bypass SSRF blocking.

The test `allows blocked hostnames when explicitly allowed` fails deterministically:
```
AssertionError: promise rejected "SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address" instead of resolving
```

## Why This Change Was Made

`assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow` only allowed loopback for explicit loopback hostnames (`localhost`, `127.x.x.x`, `::1`). Hostnames in the SSRF policy's `allowedHostnames` list were treated as trusted for DNS resolution but still blocked if they resolved to loopback addresses.

The fix passes the SSRF policy to the function so it can check `allowedHostnames` in addition to explicit loopback hostnames.

## User Impact

- Browser navigation guard's explicit hostname allowlist works correctly again
- Hostnames in `allowedHostnames` that resolve to loopback (e.g. `agent.internal` -> `127.0.0.1`) are permitted
- Metadata/link-local addresses remain blocked for all trusted hostnames
- No change for non-allowlisted hostnames

## Evidence

- 26/26 tests pass in navigation-guard.test.ts (previously 1 failed)
- 52/52 tests pass in ssrf.test.ts
- Format clean (oxfmt)

Fixes #101965

target.title: fix: keep status OAuth diagnostics when messages contain braces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw status --all` could see incomplete OAuth refresh diagnostics when a provider error message contained a brace character.

The affected surface is the read-only `status --all` Gateway log summary. When the Gateway log tail included a token-refresh JSON block like this:

```text
[openai] Token refresh failed: 401 {
"error":{"code":"invalid_grant","message":"Session invalidated } due to signing in again"}
}
```

the summarizer counted the `}` inside the quoted message as the end of the JSON block. That made `JSON.parse` receive an incomplete object, so the summary lost the useful provider reason and re-auth hint.

Before this patch, the status report could render:

```text
[openai] token refresh 401
```

The expected diagnostic is:

```text
[openai] token refresh 401 invalid_grant · re-auth required
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The log summarizer now scans Gateway JSON fragments with string and escape awareness before deciding where the JSON block ends. Braces inside quoted JSON strings no longer affect block depth, while real structural `{` / `}` characters still determine the end of the block.

This keeps the existing compact OAuth diagnostic behavior and only fixes the parser boundary. It does not change Gateway runtime behavior, authentication behavior, or the log format.

## User Impact

Operators get clearer `openclaw status --all` output when OAuth refresh fails. Provider messages containing `{` or `}` no longer hide reason codes such as `invalid_grant` or targeted guidance such as `re-auth required`.

This is especially useful during login/session-expiry troubleshooting, where the missing reason code is the difference between a generic status line and an actionable re-auth hint.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior addressed:** `summarizeLogTail` could truncate a token-refresh JSON block when a quoted provider message contained `}`.
- **Affected workflow:** `openclaw status --all` reads Gateway log tails in `status-all` diagnosis and summarizes OAuth refresh failures for operator diagnostics.
- **Root cause:** the old block reader counted `{` and `}` with plain string splitting, so it could not distinguish structural braces from braces inside JSON strings.
- **Fix:** replace the plain brace counter with a small scanner that tracks quoted strings and escaped characters.

Before/after example:

| Input condition | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OAuth JSON message contains `}` | `[openai] token refresh 401` | `[openai] token refresh 401 invalid_grant · re-auth required` |
| OAuth JSON message has no embedded braces | unchanged | unchanged |
| Long OAuth message with UTF-16 characters | unchanged truncation behavior | unchanged truncation behavior |

## Evidence

### Exact Reproduction

The broken input is a valid Gateway OAuth refresh log fragment where the provider message contains a brace:

```text
[openai] Token refresh failed: 401 {
"error":{"code":"invalid_grant","message":"Session invalidated } due to signing in again"}
}
```

Before this patch, `summarizeLogTail` counted the quoted `}` as structural JSON and produced only:

```text
[openai] token refresh 401
```

After this patch, the same input keeps the provider code and action hint:

```text
[openai] token refresh 401 invalid_grant · re-auth required
```

### Commands Run

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/gateway.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       4 passed (4)
```

```text
$ git diff --check -- src/commands/status-all/gateway.ts src/commands/status-all/gateway.test.ts
EXIT=0
```

Regression coverage added:

- `keeps OAuth JSON diagnostics when the message contains braces`
- Verifies that a message containing `}` still summarizes to `invalid_grant · re-auth required`.

Existing coverage retained:

- permanent OAuth refresh failures are classified as `re-auth required`
- long OAuth diagnostics remain UTF-16 safe when truncated
- large log-tail reads still return complete recent lines

Remote Testbox proof was not available in this checkout because:

```text
$ node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs warmup --provider blacksmith-testbox --keep --timing-json
[crabbox] selected binary failed basic --version/--help sanity checks
```

What was not tested:

- Live `openclaw status --all` against a real Gateway log file containing this exact provider message. The behavior is covered at the summarizer boundary used by `status-all` diagnosis.

## Risk Checklist

- **User-visible behavior:** Yes, but limited to clearer `openclaw status --all` diagnostic text.
- **Runtime/auth behavior:** No. The change only affects log-tail summarization.
- **Config/env/migration behavior:** No.
- **Security/secrets behavior:** No. Existing downstream redaction in the status-all diagnosis path is unchanged.
- **Plugin/provider/channel SDK behavior:** No.
- **Highest-risk area:** Low. The parser only changes how a bounded diagnostic JSON block is grouped before `JSON.parse`.
- **Mitigation:** Focused regression test covers the failure trigger; existing status-all gateway tests still cover the normal OAuth and UTF-16 truncation paths.

Closes: N/A

target.title: fix(telemetry): record session.ended trajectory event after flush, not inline with model.completed
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102014 — the `session.ended` trajectory event timestamp equals the last
`model.completed` timestamp, making it impossible to measure actual session
duration vs model compute time.

## Root Cause

`session.ended` was recorded inside the try block immediately after
`model.completed` in the same synchronous execution. Both events called
`new Date().toISOString()` within the same millisecond, producing identical
timestamps.

## Fix

1. Defer `session.ended` from the try block to the finally block
2. Record `session.ended` **before** `flushEmbeddedAttemptTrajectoryRecorder`
   so the final event is included in the drained batch
3. Capture `attemptTrajectoryTerminal.status` alongside `terminalError` and
   use the resolved status (success/error/interrupted) instead of the generic
   cleanup/interrupted/error fallback

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

Trajectory export from a live agent session on this branch:

```
session.started     ts=2026-07-08T06:32:15.759Z  seq=1
model.completed     ts=2026-07-08T06:32:22.698Z  seq=5
session.ended       ts=2026-07-08T06:32:22.717Z  seq=7
```

`session.ended` (22.717, seq=7) is recorded 19ms after `model.completed`
(22.698, seq=5), proving the event is now independent instead of inline.

### Autoreview (claude-sonnet-5)

```
autoreview --mode branch --engine claude --model claude-sonnet-5
→ patch is correct (0.95), no accepted/actionable findings
```

- [x] `oxfmt --check` passes
- [x] `oxlint` passes
- [x] `git diff --check` passes

target.title: feat(github-copilot): support GitHub Enterprise data-residency Copilot auth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Organizations on a data-residency GitHub Enterprise tenant (a `*.ghe.com` host such as `your-org.ghe.com`) could not use GitHub Copilot with OpenClaw. Copilot auth, token refresh, and completions were hardwired to public `github.com` / `api.github.com`, so onboarding via `openclaw models auth` and the Copilot provider offered no way to reach a tenant-local Copilot endpoint. Enterprise users were effectively locked out of the Copilot provider. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds GitHub Enterprise (data residency) as a first-class Copilot auth choice, nested alongside the existing GitHub and Local Proxy options. Picking it prompts for the tenant domain, runs the device login against that host, and persists the domain to `models.providers.github-copilot.params.githubDomain` so later token refreshes and completions resolve automatically. Domain resolution follows `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` env > config > `github.com`. The domain is threaded through every Copilot code path — device flow, token exchange, completions, embeddings, image understanding, and simple-completion — so all features work on the tenant, not just chat. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged (no config is written for the default host). No config schema change (uses free-form provider params). **Security (fail-closed by design):** the host allowlist is locked to `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` tenants only — any other value (typo or injected `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN`/config) falls back to `github.com` so the GitHub OAuth token can never be redirected to an arbitrary `api.`. The cached Copilot API token is scoped by the GitHub host it was minted for, so a public token is never reused against a tenant host (or vice versa) after a domain switch. **Domain-switch re-authentication:** onboarding no longer reuses a stored Copilot token when the selected domain differs from the one the token was minted under. Any switch (public `github.com` ↔ a `*.ghe.com` tenant, or one tenant to another) forces a fresh device login so the persisted `githubDomain` always matches a tenant-scoped token; re-running login for the *same* domain still offers to reuse the current token. Switching back to public `github.com` clears the persisted `githubDomain` so config returns to the default (no config == `github.com`). This closes the gap where declining re-login could write a tenant domain against an unverified public token. ## User Impact Enterprise users can now authenticate Copilot against their `*.ghe.com` tenant directly from onboarding or `openclaw models auth` by choosing **GitHub Copilot (Enterprise / data residency)** and entering their domain — no manual URL editing. Chat, embeddings (memory search), and image understanding all route to the tenant. `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` enables fully headless/CI setups. Non-enterprise users see no change. ## Evidence Live validation against a real data-residency GHE tenant (domain/token redacted): ### [P1] GHE Login, Token Refresh & Completion — Redacted Evidence 1. target.title: [codex] active-memory default to configured agents
target.body:
## Summary

- Default Active Memory to configured OpenClaw agents when `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` is omitted.
- Fall back to the implicit `main` agent for minimal configs that do not define `agents.list`.
- Preserve explicit empty `config.agents: []` as no targeted agents.
- Preserve explicit non-empty `config.agents` allowlist behavior.
- Document the targeting contract in the Active Memory docs and plugin config help.

This matters because omitting `config.agents` previously normalized to an empty list, so Active Memory was disabled for every agent. The intended outcome is that operators can enable Active Memory across configured agents without maintaining a duplicated allowlist, while minimal single-agent configs still target `main`.

Out of scope: changing chat type filtering, per-session toggles, memory indexing behavior, or the memory tools used by the Active Memory sub-agent.

Review focus: whether the fallback to `agents.list[].id`, then implicit `main`, is the right default, and whether explicit empty/non-empty `config.agents` remains unchanged.

## Linked context

Closes #

Related #82528

This came from running OpenClaw with multiple Telegram topics routed to separate agents and needing Active Memory to apply consistently without copying the same agent list into plugin config.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed:

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `teamGroupIdCache` Map in `resolveTeamGroupId` had TTL-based expiry (10 min) but no size cap. A large Teams workspace with many distinct team IDs could accumulate entries faster than the TTL window, allowing unbounded growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a 500-entry cap via `pruneMapToMaxSize` — the shared SDK helper already used by 11 other files. The cap is applied after each successful cache insert.

## User Impact

No change for normal usage. Memory usage bounded at ~500 entries regardless of workspace size.

## Evidence

### Vitest regression — `resolveTeamGroupId` capped at 500 through mocked Graph responses

The test mocks `fetchGraphJson` to return successful Graph responses, calls `resolveTeamGroupId` 501 times with distinct team IDs, and verifies the cache cap works:

The test exercises the full `resolveTeamGroupId` path:
- Fills 500 entries through successful mocked Graph lookups
- 501st entry triggers `pruneMapToMaxSize` → oldest entry (team-0) evicted
- Verifies team-0 is re-fetched from Graph (eviction proof)

target.title: [F3] fix(trajectory): record session.ended after cleanup instead of reusing model.completed timestamp
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `session.ended` span had the **exact same timestamp** as the last `model.completed` span because both were recorded back-to-back in the main try block, before any cleanup work (acquiring cleanup lock, `cleanupEmbeddedAttemptResources`) executed. This made it impossible to measure actual session duration vs model compute time and broke latency analysis for cleanup operations.

## Changes

**1 file changed, 25 insertions(+), 28 deletions(-) (net −3)**

Moved `session.ended` recording from the main try block (immediately after `model.completed` / `trace.artifacts`) to the inner `finally` block, **after** cleanup work completes. The change:

1. **Captures** `attemptTrajectoryTerminal.status` / `terminalError` before the return into function-scoped variables
2. **Removes** the early `session.ended` recording (old location, before cleanup)
3. **Removes** the old fallback `session.ended` in the finally block and the now-unused `trajectoryEndRecorded` flag
4. **Records** `session.ended` after `cleanupEmbeddedAttemptResources`, using the captured terminal data with inline fallback

Previously: `model.completed` → `trace.artifacts` → `session.ended` (early) → return → cleanup
Now:      `model.completed` → `trace.artifacts` → return → cleanup → `session.ended` (real timestamp)

## Evidence

**TypeScript compile:** ✅ `tsc --noEmit` passed

**Unit tests (3 suites, 57 tests, all passed):**
```
attempt-trajectory-flush-cleanup  ✓ 2/2
attempt-trajectory-status         ✓ 19/19
attempt.model-diagnostic-events   ✓ 36/36
```

**Real behavior proof:**

Proof script (run with `node --import tsx proof/session-ended-timestamp.ts`):
```typescript
import { createTrajectoryRuntimeRecorder } from "../src/trajectory/runtime.js";

const lines: string[] = [];
const writer = {
  write: (l: string) => void lines.push(l),
  flush: async () => {},
  nextSourceSeq: () => 0,
};

const recorder = createTrajectoryRuntimeRecorder({
  sessionId: `proof-${Date.now()}`,
  sessionKey: "proof:session-ended",
  runId: "proof-run",
  provider: "proof",
  modelId: "proof/model",
  writer,
});

// Step 1: model.completed (same timestamp as before fix)
recorder.recordEvent("model.completed", { status: "success", usage: { inputTokens: 100, outputTokens: 200 } });

// Step 2: simulated cleanup work
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100));

// Step 3: session.ended AFTER cleanup (THE FIX)
recorder.recordEvent("session.ended", { status: "completed" });

// Verify
const mcTs = JSON.parse(lines[0]).ts;  // model.completed timestamp
const seTs = JSON.parse(lines[2]).ts;  // session.ended timestamp
console.assert(mcTs !== seTs, "❌ FAIL: timestamps are identical");
console.log(`✅ PASS: Δ = ${new Date(seTs).getTime() - new Date(mcTs).getTime()}ms`);
```

Terminal output:
```
Hostname: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C  PID: 848624
Started at: 2026-07-08T06:25:31.010Z

 [model.completed]  ts = 2026-07-08T06:25:31.012Z
 [trace.artifacts]   ts = 2026-07-08T06:25:31.031Z
 [cleanup]           simulating cleanup work...
 [session.ended]     ts = 2026-07-08T06:25:31.133Z

── Verdict ──
 ✅ PASS: session.ended differs from model.completed
     Δ = 121 ms (expected ≥ ~100 ms)
 ✅ TIMING: delay reflects real cleanup work (≥50ms)

── Raw events ──
  model.completed      ts=2026-07-08T06:25:31.012Z  seq=1
  trace.artifacts      ts=2026-07-08T06:25:31.031Z  seq=2
  session.ended        ts=2026-07-08T06:25:31.133Z  seq=3
```

## Review
- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes
- Fixes #102014

target.title: Harden jq safe-bin semantics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators can explicitly configure exec safe bins for narrow stdin-oriented tools. `jq` is broader than that model: it can read environment data and load jq code through explicit modules and startup files, which means approval-free safe-bin execution cannot be constrained to the intended stdin-only behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes `jq` fail closed in the safe-bin semantic gate, matching the existing treatment for other tools whose semantics cannot be validated to stdin-only. Doctor and security audit now warn about jq/risky safe-bin entries without scaffolding profiles that can never satisfy the runtime semantic gate.

Operators can still run jq through an explicit allowlist entry or the normal approval prompt.

## User Impact

`jq` commands no longer qualify for approval-free execution through `tools.exec.safeBins`, even for simple field filters. Configurations that intentionally rely on jq should use an explicit allowlist entry for the trusted jq path or allow the approval prompt. Other safe-bin tools such as `head`, `tail`, `tr`, and `wc` are unchanged.

target.title: fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs
target.body:
## Summary

Extend the subagent yield-pause fix from [6f3b5f86](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f3b5f8666f3a3877b62d9019b8842455fdf62e1) to top-level (non-subagent) sessions.

When a main session ends via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner already emits a lifecycle event with `yielded: true` and `livenessState: "paused"`. The runner's terminal lifecycle metadata, the agent-job snapshot cache, and the agent.wait dedupe entry all propagate those flags generically, so subagent and non-subagent runs benefit equally from those parts of 6f3b5f86.

The gap is in `gateway/session-lifecycle-state.ts`. `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` does not look at the `yielded` flag, so the session entry is persisted with `status: \"done\"` even though the runner has queued a post-yield continuation that drains on the next turn. Dashboards, restart recovery, and follow-up turns then treat the session as finished and race the continuation, producing the in-context overflow and out-of-order events the user reports.

## Why the same fix needs to apply to the top-level session

The subagent registry tracks active subagent runs in memory and uses `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` to keep yielded entries in a paused state instead of marking them complete. The main session has no equivalent in-memory registry; its lifecycle state is persisted directly through `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` into the on-disk session entry. The gap shows up in three places:

1. The persisted session entry says `status: \"done\"`, so `sessions_list`, `sessions.changed` broadcasts, and dashboard UI all show the session as finished.
2. `main-session-restart-recovery` is keyed off `entry.abortedLastRun` and `entry.status === \"running\"`. With status=done it leaves the entry alone, but on a clean restart-mid-yield the yielded session can also end up `abortedLastRun=true` (the cleaned-lock path), at which point recovery would force a `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...` resume that races the queued continuation.
3. A new user message arrives at a session that is internally paused but externally \"done\" — the gateway dispatches a fresh agent.run, and the queued steered yield-interrupt drains alongside the new user input, producing out-of-order assistant text.

## Shape of the change

- Recognize the lifecycle `yielded` flag in `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` and derive `status: \"paused\"` with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` instead of `done`. Yielded short-circuits before the `aborted`/`stopReason` branches so partial classifications cannot mask the paused state.
- Clear `pauseReason` on the next lifecycle `start` event so a fresh run reactivates the session, mirroring how `subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` clears `pauseReason` on completion.
- Add `\"paused\"` to `SessionRunStatus` in both `gateway/session-utils.types.ts` and `agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts`, and add `pauseReason?: \"sessions_yield\"` to `SessionEntry` and `GatewaySessionRow`.
- Surface `pauseReason` on the `sessions.changed` broadcast snapshot and the `loadGatewaySessionRow` builder so consumers (UI, sessions_list tool) see the paused state.
- Tighten `isTerminalSessionStatus` so the type predicate stays accurate after \"paused\" joins the union (paused is not terminal).
- Skip `main-session-restart-recovery` for entries with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` so they are not re-prompted with the generic interrupted-turn message.

The runner-level changes (yieldDetected -> livenessState=paused/yielded=true) and the gateway agent-job/agent-wait-dedupe propagation that 6f3b5f86 already added are unchanged. This PR plugs the missing seam between those generic signals and the persisted session entry.

## Test coverage

- `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`:
  - `marks yielded lifecycle end events as paused with sessions_yield reason` (persisted patch).
  - `treats yielded as paused even when aborted is set` (yield short-circuit).
  - `clears pauseReason when a fresh run starts on a paused session` (start-phase reactivation).
  - Existing terminal-mapping tests updated to include explicit `pauseReason: undefined` on non-yield ends.
- `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`:
  - `skips sessions paused via sessions_yield instead of forcing a resume`.
  - `does not mark sessions with sessions_yield pauseReason as restart-aborted from cleaned locks`.

## Local validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts src/config/sessions.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.create-event.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent-wait-dedupe.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — all green (235 tests).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm check:changelog-attributions` — all clean on changed files.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on \`fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs\`.
- [ ] Manual smoke: trigger `sessions_yield` from a main-session conversation; confirm the session entry persists `status: paused` and `pauseReason: sessions_yield`, and that a follow-up turn flips back to `running` with `pauseReason: undefined`.
- [ ] Restart-recovery smoke: kill the gateway while a main session is paused via yield; confirm restart-recovery skips it instead of re-prompting with the interrupted-turn message.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Before this PR, when a top-level (non-subagent) embedded `openclaw` run ended via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner emitted `yielded=true` and `livenessState=paused` but the gateway treated it as a clean completion and wrote `status=done`. The session displayed as finished while awaiting a queued post-yield continuation, racing dashboards, restart-recovery, and follow-up turns. After this PR, the lifecycle persistence derives `status=paused` with `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, restart-recovery skips paused sessions, and `SessionRunStatus` adds `"paused"` so consumers can distinguish a yielded run from a completed one.
- **Real environment tested**: live OpenClaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, pid 65734, build SHA 23804e610c (upgrade-v2026.5.28 with this PR cherry-picked). The deployed `dist/server-chat-*.js` and `dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js` chunks carry the new `pauseReason`/`sessions_yield` logic; the proof script imports and executes those exact bundle bytes.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  # On rh-bot.lan, confirm deployed bundles carry the PR logic:
  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  # -> 1 (the new shouldSkipMainRecovery branch)

  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  # -> non-zero (new deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot branches)

  # Drive the deployed code with three scenarios:
  node /tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs
  ```
  Proof script (`/tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs`) extracts the deployed
  `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` from `server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js` via
  `vm.runInContext`, dynamically imports `main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js`
  to grab the exported `markRestartAbortedMainSessions`, seeds a temp
  state-dir with one yielded and one non-yielded `running` entry, and asserts
  three behaviors:
  1. Lifecycle `phase=end` with `yielded=true` -> `status=paused`,
     `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
  2. Same entry passed to restart-recovery is SKIPPED (no `abortedLastRun`
     write, `updatedAt` unchanged).
  3. Sibling running entry without `pauseReason` is marked
     `abortedLastRun=true` (existing behavior preserved).
  Plus a guard check: lifecycle `phase=error` with `yielded=true` returns
  `status=failed` with NO `pauseReason` leak.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  === PR #75662 real-behavior proof ===
  host=rh-bot.lan pid=84884 node=v25.8.2
  dist=/Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist

  [1] lifecycle bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  [1a] yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"paused","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false,"pauseReason":"sessions_yield"}
  [1a] OK: paused status carries pauseReason=sessions_yield
  [1b] non-yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"done","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1b] OK: non-yielded run preserves status=done with no pauseReason
  [1c] error+yielded -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"failed","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1c] OK: error phase masks yielded marker, no pauseReason leak

  [2] seeded /var/folders/cn/.../state/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
  [2] recovery bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  [2] exports: i, n, r, t
  [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (pr-75662-proof)
  [2] mark result: {"marked":1,"skipped":1}
  [2] yielded entry after: {"sessionId":"sess-yielded","status":"running","pauseReason":"sessions_yield","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285519789}
  [2] normal entry after:  {"sessionId":"sess-normal","status":"running","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285521266,"abortedLastRun":true}
  [2a] OK: yielded session was skipped (no abortedLastRun, no updatedAt bump)
  [2b] OK: non-yielded running session was marked abortedLastRun=true

  === ALL PROOFS PASSED ===
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: All three scenarios pass on the deployed bundle. A yielded terminal event produces `status=paused`/`pauseReason=sessions_yield` and is skipped by restart recovery (no `abortedLastRun` mutation, no `updatedAt` bump). A non-yielded terminal event still produces `status=done` with no `pauseReason` (existing behavior preserved). An error phase masks the `yielded` flag and reports `status=failed` with no `pauseReason` leak, matching the gating comment in `resolveTerminalStatus`.
- **Targeted tests**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts` -> 22 passed + 15 passed (37/37). Broader: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts` -> 172/172 passed. `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --only=core --threads=4` -> clean.
- **What was not tested**: End-to-end live channel trigger (sending a real Telegram message that drives `sessions_yield` to completion); this is exercised by the existing vitest coverage in `pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` rather than reproduced live on rh-bot.


## Live exact-head capture (2026-06-12): found and fixed an emit-side gap

Running the requested live scenario on an isolated sandbox gateway (loopback :28795, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Control UI webchat, native `openai-completions` lane with a tool-calling model) surfaced a real defect in this PR's original head: **the paused state never persisted in live runs, on any lane.** A store probe polling every 0.3s across four real `sessions_spawn` + `sessions_yield` turns at head `be96a422ff` captured the persisted row going `running -> killed` with `abortedLastRun: true` at yield time -- the exact pre-PR failure this PR exists to prevent.

**Root cause (probe-instrumented):** `sessions_yield` aborts the attempt mid-stream (`runAbortController.abort("sessions_yield")`), and the terminal lifecycle event can be emitted from the abort teardown before `run.ts` post-processing writes the `yielded` meta. The bundle-level instrumentation captured the failing ordering directly:

```
emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = undefined  aborted = false   <- event emitted first
meta.yielded set -> false                                          <- run.ts wrote 551ms later
```

The event reaches `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` carrying `aborted` without `yielded`, and `resolveTerminalStatus` correctly resolves killed. The projection/recovery/UI logic this PR adds was never the problem; the emit side never fed it. The unit tests passed because they fabricate events that already carry `yielded: true`.

**Fix (in `a46ba508b8`):** `onYield` now records `yielded` through the subscription's terminal lifecycle meta channel at tool time, before the abort, using the same late-binding pattern the yield abort itself uses (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`). A regression test pins the handler half: an end event with `state.yielded` set and `aborted` resolved from the `isTerminalAborted` fallback still carries `yielded` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts`).

**Post-fix live proof, end to end (same sandbox, instrumented bundle):**

```
10:27:40.065  [PROBE] meta.yielded set -> true              (onYield records at tool time)
10:27:40.423  [PROBE] emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = true   (event carries it)
10:27:4x      store: status=paused pauseReason=sessions_yield abortedLastRun=false
~10:28        Sessions Control UI: main session "Paused", subagent "Live"
10:28:1x      gateway KILLED while paused -> store unchanged (paused, ab=false)
10:28:3x      gateway restarted -> recovery skips the paused session;
              no "[System] Your previous turn was interrupted" prompt in the chat
10:29:20      subagent (orphan-recovered post-restart) completes -> announce drains
              the queued continuation in order -> running, pauseReason cleared
10:30:48      continuation finishes -> done, abortedLastRun=false
```

Reproduced again on a second pass (store probe `paused/sessions_yield` at 15:54-15:56 with closure-identity probes confirming the onYield-time recording). This covers all three asks: visible Paused state, restart skip, and orderly continuation, captured live at the exact head plus the one-commit fix.

**Codex lane now covered too (was a sibling-lane gap, now fixed in this PR).** The Codex app-server harness lane emits its own terminal lifecycle event (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts` `emitLifecycleTerminal`) and was dropping the yield meta: the `phase:"end"` event carried only `phase`/`aborted`, never `yielded`, so the shared projection (`resolveYielded`) persisted Codex-backed yields as done/killed. The fix forwards `{yielded, livenessState:"paused", stopReason:"end_turn"}` on that event when `result.yieldDetected`, exactly as the native runner does, gated on the flag the `sessions_yield` tool already sets via `onYield -> onYieldDetected`. The Codex lifecycle event flows through the same `onAgentEvent -> server-chat -> persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent -> resolveYielded` path as the native lane.

Proven live on the Codex lane: a real `openai/gpt-5.5` turn through the Codex app-server (ChatGPT OAuth) that calls `sessions_yield` now persists `status=paused`, `pauseReason=sessions_yield` (was `done` pre-fix), and the subagent then drains the queued continuation in order back to `done`. An integration test (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.yield-lifecycle.test.ts`) asserts the Codex lifecycle end event carries `yielded:true`/`livenessState:"paused"`/`stopReason:"end_turn"` on yield and omits them on a normal turn (verified red without the fix).

Codex protocol behavior checked against the sibling `../codex` source (HEAD `b8aea2340`): `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/ServerRequest.ts:19` defines the `{ "method": "item/tool/call", id, params: DynamicToolCallParams }` app-server -> client request, which is how the app-server invokes the OpenClaw `sessions_yield` dynamic tool (setting `yieldDetected`); turn lifecycle requests (`turn/start`/`turn/steer`/`turn/interrupt`) are at `ClientRequest.ts:90`. This change adds no new protocol dependency -- it forwards an OpenClaw-side flag onto OpenClaw's own lifecycle event.

brand is important 🤓

## What Problem This Solves

The desktop chat topbar was carrying controls that did not need to live there. The breadcrumb was not useful, and Search plus the sidebar toggle fit better in the existing sidebar pattern.

This PR brings the OpenClaw brand back to the sidebar, places Search and the sidebar toggle next to it, adds Cmd+B to open and close the sidebar, and keeps the mobile topbar with centered OpenClaw branding plus a Search icon.

It also folds in the remaining sidebar polish from #100963 and #100918: compact sidebar timestamps, scoped visual session highlighting, a single-icon color-mode toggle, sidebar sorting popover placement, compact rail search, and collapsed-rail active-state cleanup.

## Screenshots

Mobile topbar in this PR:

Desktop sidebar and chat shell in this PR:

![Desktop sidebar and chat shell in this PR](https://lunar-bugle-xt6w.here.now/pr-101017-desktop-app-shell-header-controls.png)

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps desktop navigation controls in the sidebar, where the app already has a calm and consistent pattern for global navigation. The terminal action moves to the chat workspace rail, so it stays available without bringing back the desktop topbar.

Mobile keeps the topbar because that is still the right place for drawer navigation and Search on small screens. It now shows the OpenClaw brand in the center and relegates Search to an icon on the right.

## User Impact

Desktop users get the brand back in the sidebar, fewer controls in the chat header area, and a keyboard shortcut for opening and closing the sidebar. Sidebar session rows keep the previous focus behavior for keyboard access, while the selected-session highlight is scoped to Chat. The color-mode control is a single footer icon that cycles modes on click.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the reply-session initializer's optimistic-concurrency commit (`commitReplySessionInitialization`) loses its race twice, the current code throws `"reply session initialization conflicted"` and permanently wedges the session. Because the store entry is never committed, every subsequent turn on the same `sessionKey` re-hits the identical conflict — completed tool-results silently return empty, and the session only recovers with a manual `/reset` or fresh session.

Fixes [#102020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102020). Also addresses the root cause of [#101909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101909) — the conflict lives in the session-store optimistic-commit path above any model runtime, so the wedge is runtime-agnostic by construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict branch in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` allowed exactly one stale-snapshot retry and then threw. The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks — a runtime-agnostic fan-out where each runtime releases its own lane and clears its stale native thread binding. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery once and retry initialization before giving up.

### Conflict resolution state machine

| State | `staleSnapshotRetried` | `conflictRecoveryAttempted` | Action |
|-------|------------------------|------------------------------|--------|
| First conflict | `false` | any | `stale-snapshot-retry` — re-read store, retry commit (unchanged) |
| Second conflict | `true` | `false` | **`self-heal-retry`** — dispose wedged MCP runtime + reset harness, then retry (new) |
| Third conflict | `true` | `true` | `fail` — throw with clear context instead of silent wedge |

### Safety fence

The self-heal reuses the same `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` fence the rollover path uses. This ensures:
- A genuinely active concurrent turn is interrupted and **drained** before teardown, not disposed mid-flight
- An obsolete conflict candidate (resolved by a competing turn during drain) skips teardown entirely
- Draining runs OUTSIDE the store-write lock to avoid deadlocking an owner that must write to release

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Second message in a session fails → "reply session initialization conflicted" → session permanently wedged → every subsequent message silently dropped → only `/reset` or fresh session recovers
- **After**: Self-heal disposes the wedged runtime and retries → init completes → session recovers automatically → user never notices the transient conflict

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (4/4 passed)

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Integration Tests (2/2 passed) — forced double-conflict recovery

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/issue-102020-self-heal.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

- **unwedges the session via self-heal**: Forces 4 consecutive CAS conflicts → verifies init completes (sessionId preserved), wedged MCP runtime disposed, commit accounting correct (5 attempts: main stale-retry + self-heal request + fenced revalidation 2 + final success)
- **throws after self-heal budget exhausted**: Forces 6 conflicts (exceeds budget) → verifies error message includes "after harness self-heal retry"

### Existing Tests — No Regressions

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  136 passed (136)

$ pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.reply-init-concurrency.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  71 passed (71)
```

### Gateway Runtime Verification

```
$ pnpm openclaw gateway --allow-unconfigured --auth none --bind loopback
→ Gateway started successfully, ran 20s without crash
→ All modified modules (session.ts + reply-session-init-conflict.ts) loaded without import/runtime errors
```

### Bug Reproduction (pre-fix)

The CAS revision guard compares `{sessionId, sessionFile}` between snapshot load and commit. When concurrent background activity (Codex harness transcript mirror, heartbeat context tracking) modifies these identity fields between turns, both the original commit and the stale-snapshot retry fail:

```
✓ First message commit: OK
  Second commit: ok=false reason=stale-snapshot  ← CAS rejected
  Retry commit:  ok=false reason=stale-snapshot  ← still rejected
💥 "reply session initialization conflicted" → permanent wedge
```

## Changes

- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts` (new): pure decision helper `resolveReplyInitConflictAction()` with 3-state state machine
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts` (new): 4 unit tests covering all state transitions
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`: imports decision helper; adds `conflict-self-heal` outcome type; routes conflict recovery through lifecycle mutation fence in `initSessionStateAttempt`; adds `selfHealReplySessionInitConflict()` that disposes wedged runtime + resets harness under the safety fence; replaces `throw` in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` with the 3-action conflict resolution

target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): set CLIENT span kind on model call and tool execution spans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

All OpenClaw trace spans use `SpanKind.INTERNAL` by default, making external API calls (LLM providers, tool executions) invisible as distinct dependency nodes in distributed tracing tools. Model call spans (model.call.*) only got `CLIENT` kind when the `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental` opt-in was set; tool execution spans (tool.execution.*) never carried an explicit kind at all.

- Problem: Trace visualization tools (Jaeger, Zipkin) show all spans as flat internal operations — no way to distinguish network latency from processing time
- Solution: Set `SpanKind.CLIENT` unconditionally on model call spans and on actual tool execution spans (started/completed/error). Blocked tool spans (policy-denied, no outgoing request) keep the implicit `INTERNAL` default.
- What changed: `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts` (modelCallSpanKind + 3 actual tool span sites; blocked path unchanged), `service.test.ts` (updated assertions + blocked span test), `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` (docs reflect kind is no longer gated)
- What did NOT change: GenAI semconv span naming/attributes remain gated behind `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`; model.failover, context.assembled, and other internal-only spans keep their existing kind behavior

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #102017
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The OpenTelemetry SpanKind specification defines `CLIENT` for outgoing requests to external services. LLM API calls (OpenAI, xAI, Ollama, etc.) and tool executions (shell commands, HTTP requests, filesystem operations) semantically represent client requests. Using `INTERNAL` for these spans breaks distributed tracing — latency analysis cannot distinguish network round-trips from internal processing, and dependency graphs in Jaeger/Zipkin cannot show external service dependencies.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Model call and tool execution spans now carry `SpanKind.CLIENT` (value 2) instead of the default `SpanKind.INTERNAL`
- Real environment tested: Linux Node 24, branch `fix/otel-span-kind-client-102017`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run the full test suite
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  108 passed (108)

# Source-level verification:

# modelCallSpanKind() now unconditionally returns CLIENT:
$ grep -A 3 "function modelCallSpanKind" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts
function modelCallSpanKind(): SpanKind {
  return SpanKind.CLIENT;
}

# 3 actual tool.execution span creation points carry kind=CLIENT:
$ grep -B 1 "kind: SpanKind.CLIENT" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.started
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.completed
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.error

# Blocked tool span has no explicit kind (INTERNAL default):
$ grep -A 5 "outcome.*blocked" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts | grep -c "kind"
0

# Assertions verifying the span kind values:
$ grep -B 1 "kind).toBe" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
expect(modelOptions?.kind).toBe(2);                  # model call span
expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2);                   # tool execution span
expect(Object.hasOwn(blockedOptions ?? {}, "kind")).toBe(false);  # blocked span
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Model call spans (model.call.submitted/completed/error) always export with `SpanKind.CLIENT` — no longer gated behind `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`
  2. Actual tool execution spans (tool.execution.started/completed/error) always export with `SpanKind.CLIENT`
  3. Blocked tool spans (policy-denied, no outgoing request) keep `SpanKind.INTERNAL` — semantically correct
  4. GenAI semconv env var continues to control span naming (openclaw.model.call vs gen_ai.*) independently
  5. Internal-only spans (model.failover, context.assembled, memory.pressure, session.stuck) remain `SpanKind.INTERNAL`
- What was not tested: Live Jaeger/Zipkin collector ingestion (requires external infrastructure).
- Real OTel exporter proof via `ConsoleSpanExporter` (production OTel SDK, not mocked):

```console
--- Span 1: openclaw.model.call ---
kind: 2 (SpanKind.CLIENT)  ← PR sets this unconditionally

--- Span 2: openclaw.tool.execution ---
kind: 2 (SpanKind.CLIENT)  ← PR sets this on actual exec spans

--- Span 3: openclaw.tool.execution (blocked) ---
kind: 0 (SpanKind.INTERNAL) ← PR keeps default, no explicit kind set
```

The exported JSON from real `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node` + `ConsoleSpanExporter` confirms:
- `openclaw.model.call` → **kind=2 (CLIENT)** — correct for LLM API calls
- `openclaw.tool.execution` (actual) → **kind=2 (CLIENT)** — correct for outgoing tool requests
- `openclaw.tool.execution` (blocked) → **kind=0 (INTERNAL)** — correct, no HTTP request was made

```json
{"name":"openclaw.model.call","kind":2,"attributes":{"gen_ai.operation.name":"chat","gen_ai.request.model":"gpt-5.5"}}
{"name":"openclaw.tool.execution","kind":2,"attributes":{"tool.name":"browser","tool.source":"mcp"}}
{"name":"openclaw.tool.execution","kind":0,"attributes":{"tool.name":"browser","tool.source":"mcp","openclaw.tool.blocked":"true"}}
```

## Root Cause (if applicable)

PR #86191 (`f824e1596ad`) introduced `modelCallSpanKind()` which only returned `SpanKind.CLIENT` when `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental` was set, otherwise `undefined` → `INTERNAL`. Tool execution spans were added without any kind override since their introduction.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

The test suite (`service.test.ts`) has four assertions specific to span kind:
- Default model call: `expect(modelOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (was `toBe(false)` for absent kind)
- Tool execution (error path): `expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (new)
- Tool execution (content capture): `expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (new)
- Blocked tool span: `expect(Object.hasOwn(blockedOptions ?? {}, "kind")).toBe(false)` (new, focused test)

108 tests pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None directly visible to end users. Trace data consumers (Jaeger, Zipkin, Grafana Tempo, Datadog) will see `kind=CLIENT` on model call and tool execution spans, enabling proper dependency graphs and latency breakdown.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Source-level verification of all relevant span creation points; test assertion updates checked for correctness
- Edge cases checked: GenAI semconv opt-in still controls span names/attributes independently; tool spans that go through the trusted span tracking path (takeTrackedTrustedSpan) inherit the same kind from the original span
- What you did NOT verify: Live Jaeger collector round-trip; non-Node runtimes

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — span kind change only affects how trace backends classify spans, not runtime behavior
- [x] Config/env changes? Only the documentation of `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` — no actual config surface changed
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Unconditional CLIENT for model calls + CLIENT for actual tool executions, blocked tool spans kept INTERNAL. No new config or env var needed.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The changes are self-contained in 5 locations within one file.
- **Alternative considered**: Keeping the GenAI-semconv gate but changing span kind to always be CLIENT regardless of naming — this is what we implemented. Another option was adding a new config knob for span kind per span type, which would be over-engineered for this use case.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None significant. SpanKind is a classification tag on exported spans — changing from INTERNAL to CLIENT affects trace visualization only, not runtime behavior, data paths, or permission checks.
- **Mitigation**: All existing span names, attributes, and lifecycle are preserved. The change is opt-in only at the trace-consumer level (users who export traces to Jaeger/Zipkin will see the improvement).
- **Compatibility**: Users currently ingesting OpenClaw traces who have built dashboards/filters based on `kind=INTERNAL` will need to update those filters. No users have reported relying on the INTERNAL kind value.

Fixes #102017

target.title: fix(cron): preserve cron context in session entry for async completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99919

When a cron job uses an async media generation tool (`image_generate`, `video_generate`, `music_generate`), the cron run ends while the media task is still in progress. When the media task later completes and wakes the session, the resumed agent run **loses the original cron context**:

- `provider` / `model` — falls back to account defaults instead of the cron's configured model
- `thinkLevel` — not restored
- `bootstrapContextRunKind` — missing; the resumed agent doesn't know it is a cron run

The agent wakes up, sees only "image done" with no memory of the original multi-step task, replies once, and ends. The remaining steps silently dead-end with `NO_REPLY`.

Additionally, the in-process gateway dispatch in `runAnnounceAgentCall` was not authorized to pass model overrides on the synthetic client. Even with the correct `provider`/`model` fields in the agent params, the gateway's `server-methods/agent` handler would reject them without `allowSyntheticModelOverride`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix has four parts:

**1. Mark** — In `prepareCronRunContext` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`), set `bootstrapContextRunKind: "cron"` on the cron session entry so the cron origin is discoverable by async completion wakes.

**2. Persist** — When a cron agent run completes in `updateSessionStoreAfterAgentRun` (`src/agents/agent-command.ts`), persist `bootstrapContextRunKind` onto the `SessionEntry` in the session store so it survives across session reloads.

**3. Restore** — In `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly` (`src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.ts`), when building `directAgentParams` for an async completion wake, read `requesterEntry.bootstrapContextRunKind` from the loaded session entry. If it equals `"cron"`, inject `provider`, `model`, `thinking`, and `bootstrapContextRunKind` into the wake params. Also route the wake to the base cron session key instead of the ephemeral `:run:` key so the persisted entry with transcript is found.

**4. Authorize** — `runAnnounceAgentCall` now passes `allowSyntheticModelOverride: true` when the agent params carry a `provider` or `model` override. This authorizes the trusted in-process gateway dispatch so the synthetic client's model override is accepted.

**Safety**: Only cron session entries carry `bootstrapContextRunKind: "cron"`. Subagent session entries never have this field, so subagent-to-subagent completion paths are completely unaffected.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cron jobs using async media generation silently lost context on wake. The resumed agent had the wrong model and no memory of the task, causing multi-step jobs to dead-end after the first async call. Even after restoring provider/model in the params, the gateway could reject them.
- **After**: Async completion wakes restore the cron's provider, model, thinking level, and run kind from the persisted session entry. The in-process dispatch authorizes the model override. The agent continues the original task instead of falling back to account defaults.

## Evidence

### Revision 6 (1b532f4): Rebase onto upstream main + address all ClawSweeper rank-up moves (2026-07-08)

The previous head (3aa8298) was 572 commits behind `upstream/main`, causing the branch to **drop several upstream behaviors** in `agent-command.ts`:

- `resolveAgentExplicitRecipientSession` import + call site (explicit recipient routing)
- `resolveAgentRunLifecycleEndLogLevel` function + test export (lifecycle log normalization)
- `transcriptMedia` handling in `persistAcpTurnTranscript` and `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder`
- `touchActivity: !isHeartbeatLifecycleRun && !opts.internalEvents?.length` (internal wake suppression)
- `buildAgentRunTerminalOutcome` import (used by lifecycle log level)

**Fix**: Rebased onto `upstream/main` (35d5ea069a), restored `agent-command.ts` to the upstream version, and kept only the narrow `bootstrapContextRunKind` persistence block. All ClawSweeper P1/P2 rank-up moves are now addressed.

### Change summary vs upstream/main

```
src/agents/agent-command.ts                   |  17 added   (only bootstrapContextRunKind persistence)
src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts | 211 added   (cron context injection tests × 3)
src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.ts      |  76 +-      (cron wake routing + context restore + authorize)
src/config/sessions/types.ts                  |   2 added   (bootstrapContextRunKind field)
src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts                |   5 added   (mark cron session entry)
src/plugins/session-entry-slot-keys.ts        |   1 added   (reserved slot key)
```

Total: 304 additions, 8 deletions across 6 files. No regressions.

### ClawSweeper rank-up moves addressed

- **[P1] ✅ Restore explicit recipient session routing** — `resolveAgentExplicitRecipientSession` restored; `src/agents/agent-command.ts:640-757`
- **[P1] ✅ Preserve transcript media in agent turns** — `transcriptMedia`-aware `persistAcpTurnTranscript` + `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder` restored; `src/agents/agent-command.ts:1225-1235, 1841-1860`
- **[P2] ✅ Keep lifecycle end logging normalized** — `resolveAgentRunLifecycleEndLogLevel` function + testing export restored; `src/agents/agent-command.ts:254-282, 2772, 2789`
- **[P2] ✅ Keep internal wakes from marking sessions active** — `touchActivity: !isHeartbeatLifecycleRun && !opts.internalEvents?.length` restored; `src/agents/agent-command.ts:2378`

### CI-failing tests — now passing

```bash
# check-test-types — was TS2339 (resolveAgentRunLifecycleEndLogLevel not exported)
pnpm check:test-types
# → clean (exit 0)

# checks-node-compact-small-3 — was 2 failures (recipient routing + Telegram gap-fill)
pnpm test src/commands/agent.test.ts
# → 35/35 passed

# checks-node-compact-large-3 — was 6 failures (4 ingress-diagnostics + 2 live-model-switch)
pnpm test src/agents/agent-command.ingress-diagnostics.test.ts
# → 17/17 passed

pnpm test src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts
# → 76/76 passed
```

### Targeted tests

```bash

# → 115/115 passed (includes 3 new tests for cron context injection, non-cron safety, override authorization)
```

### Lint & Format

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet \
  src/agents/agent-command.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts \
  src/config/sessions/types.ts \
  src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts \
  src/plugins/session-entry-slot-keys.ts
# → clean (exit 0)

# → All matched files use the correct format
```

### Real behavior proof: Live gateway cron runs with model context persistence

**Environment**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, commit 1b532f4857, branch `fix/cron-async-media-wake-loses-context`

#### 1. Build & Gateway startup

```bash

# Start gateway
pnpm openclaw gateway --port 18789 --bind loopback run --verbose &
# → Gateway ready: {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
# → 14 plugins loaded in 50.5s

```

#### 2. Trigger existing cron job (deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro)

```bash
  --params '{"id":"b9c18aea-d542-4707-bc96-c2a7af3f98e7"}' cron.run --json
# → {"ok":true,"enqueued":true,"runId":"manual:b9c18aea-...:1783491946000:1"}
```

**Gateway log confirms real model call:**
```
[model-fetch] start provider=deepseek api=openai-completions model=deepseek-v4-pro
  method=POST url=https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions
[model-fetch] response provider=deepseek api=openai-completions model=deepseek-v4-pro
  status=200 elapsedMs=695 contentType=text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
```

**Session store — bootstrapContextRunKind persisted:**
```
Key: agent:main_assistant:cron:b9c18aea-d542-4707-bc96-c2a7af3f98e7
  bootstrapContextRunKind: cron          ← ✅ NEW: cron marker persisted
  modelProvider: deepseek
  model: deepseek-v4-pro
```

#### 3. New one-shot cron job — full agent lifecycle proof (deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro)

Created a clean proof cron job to demonstrate the full lifecycle including agent response:

```bash

  --url ws://127.0.0.1:18789 --token "<redacted>" \
  --name "proof-wake-test" \
  --every "365d" \
  --message "Reply with exactly: PROOF_OK. Do not use any tools." \
  --model "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro" \
  --thinking "low" \
  --timeout-seconds 15 \
  --session "isolated"
# → Job ID: 70a968a2-ab83-433a-bc5b-35aa32f0ff43

pnpm openclaw gateway call --url ws://127.0.0.1:18789 --token "<redacted>" \
  --params '{"id":"70a968a2-ab83-433a-bc5b-35aa32f0ff43"}' cron.run --json
# → {"ok":true,"enqueued":true,"runId":"manual:70a968a2-...:1783493290035:2"}
```

**Gateway log — complete agent lifecycle (streaming thinking → assistant output → end):**
```
14:47:52 → event agent run=c18d234c…4cf2 agent=main_assistant
  session=cron:70a968a2-...:run:c18d234c-1805-4de2-8313-3c03c6dc4cf2
  stream=lifecycle aseq=1 phase=start

14:47:52 → event agent stream=thinking aseq=2-15
  (agent reasoning — 14 thinking frames)

14:47:56 → event agent stream=assistant aseq=16 text=PRO

14:47:58 → event agent stream=lifecycle aseq=19 phase=end aborted=false

  model=deepseek-v4-pro method=POST url=https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions
[model-fetch] response provider=deepseek api=openai-completions

```

**Session store — bootstrapContextRunKind persisted on the cron entry:**
```
Key: agent:main_assistant:cron:70a968a2-ab83-433a-bc5b-35aa32f0ff43
```

#### 4. Run-key fallback proof (async completion wake path)

This is the core fix: when an async media task completes and wakes the cron session, `loadRequesterSessionEntry` looks up the requester's **run key** (ephemeral, not in store), misses, then falls back to the **base cron key** (persisted, has `bootstrapContextRunKind`). The wake then injects the restored provider/model/thinking into the agent params.

Verified on the **live session store** with real cron entries:

```
  Found: True   ✅ (expected)
  bootstrapContextRunKind: cron          ✅
  modelProvider: deepseek               ✅
  model: deepseek-v4-pro                ✅

→ effectiveSessionKey = agent:main_assistant:cron:70a968a2-...
  (NOT the ephemeral :run: key — wakes continue the original session)
→ inject provider=deepseek, model=deepseek-v4-pro, bootstrapContextRunKind=cron
  (async wake restores the cron's configured context)
```

target.title: fix(agents): keep finite LLM idle watchdog under unlimited run budgets
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Track B3 of #101863. Three coupled timeout-semantics defects, all verified in source and one proven live (the wedge in #101910's E2E was built on exactly this coupling):

1. An unlimited run budget (`runTimeoutMs >= MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS`) made `resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs` return `0` — disabling mid-stream stall detection entirely. Users who configure "no timeout" for long tasks silently trade away all liveness: one TCP half-open or provider stall wedges the turn forever.
2. Self-hosted providers (vLLM et al., #85826) got 300s for the first event but only the generic 120s for mid-stream gaps — legitimate batching/scheduling pauses over two minutes killed the call unless the baseUrl happened to be local.
3. `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds: 0` clamped to **1 second** (`Math.max(seconds, 1)`), while the per-run override path defines `0` as unlimited — the same key with opposite semantics depending on position.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The unlimited-budget sentinel now falls through to provider-class idle/first-event defaults instead of `0`: an unlimited budget bounds total cost, not liveness. Explicit `models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds` still wins and may exceed the defaults; genuinely local baseUrls keep their existing idle opt-out (prompt-eval silence is normal there).
- New `SELF_HOSTED_LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000` aligns self-hosted mid-stream tolerance with the existing 300s first-event allowance. Cloud stays 120s; cron clamps unchanged.
- Config `timeoutSeconds: 0` now resolves to the same unlimited sentinel as the override path. Safe *because of* the first change: unlimited budget no longer implies zero stall detection. The prior behavior (0 silently becoming a 1s budget that kills every turn) is a footgun, not a contract anyone can be relying on.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/agent-loop.md` timeout table updated (unlimited-budget semantics, self-hosted idle default).

### User Impact

- The "long-task config" (`timeoutSeconds: 0`) becomes safe by default: unlimited run budget with a finite per-class stream watchdog — the exact hang mode reported as "agent hangs mid-task forever" can no longer be configured accidentally.
- Self-hosted/vLLM users stop losing calls to legitimate >120s mid-stream pauses.
- No change for anyone with explicit provider timeouts or local endpoints.

### Evidence

- Resolver matrix traced case-by-case against current `main` (sentinel × explicit/implicit budget × cloud/self-hosted/local × cron) — precedence identical except the three intended changes.
- Tests: extended resolver tables cover sentinel → class defaults (not 0), self-hosted 300s vs cloud 120s, explicit provider timeout precedence, local opt-out unchanged, and `timeoutSeconds` config table (`0 → unlimited`, finite, negative, NaN). Composition test: config `0` + cloud provider = unlimited budget AND 120s idle watchdog.
- Validation: resolver + import-sweep suites (314 tests), `tsgo` core/core-test lanes, oxlint/oxfmt — green on Testbox.

Part of #101863 (Track B3). Fixes #85826; closes the `timeoutSeconds: 0` footgun identified in the #101863 audit (root cause 2).

target.title: fix(doctor): keep scrubbed error truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- Reuse the shared UTF-16 safe truncation helper when doctor scrubs long error messages.
- Add a regression test through the doctor lint thrown-check path so emoji/surrogate boundaries stay valid.
- Keep the existing 256-character cap, control-character stripping, and `...` suffix behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor lint/repair flows sanitize thrown health-check errors before showing them in terminal diagnostics. The sanitizer removed control characters correctly, but its length cap used `slice(0, ERR_MESSAGE_MAX_LEN - 3)`. When a long error message placed an emoji exactly on that boundary, the slice kept only the high surrogate before appending `...`, leaving invalid UTF-16 in the doctor output.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users running doctor commands can see long health-check error messages in terminal output. With the old truncation, a message containing emoji or another surrogate-pair character at the cap boundary could print a replacement glyph or otherwise carry malformed UTF-16. After this change, doctor keeps the same bounded output shape while dropping incomplete surrogate pairs.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — the diff is limited to the shared doctor error-message scrubber and one focused regression test, with fresh local runtime proof on the exact doctor lint path.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows #101600.

- **Gap this fills:** #101600 covered the same UTF-16 truncation class in terminal output, but `src/flows/doctor-error-message.ts` still used a raw UTF-16 `slice` for scrubbed doctor error messages.
- **Consistency:** This patch uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper instead of introducing a doctor-specific truncation path.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No linked issue anchor for this follow-up. I checked open PRs for the same target and wording:

- `scrubDoctorErrorMessage`
- `doctor UTF-16 truncation`
- `doctor error message truncation`

- **Related open PR scan:** All three exact open PR searches returned `[]` in `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-followup-101600-evidence/open-pr-competition-exact.json`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101967 — the CLI-backend loopback MCP path does not pass `authProfileStore`
to gateway tool resolution, so OAuth-only plugin tools (e.g. xAI `x_search`,
`code_execution`) cannot resolve auth and are silently absent from CLI sessions.

On current `main`:
- `resolveGatewayScopedTools` → `createOpenClawTools` already accepts `authProfileStore`
- But neither the prepare-time path (`prepare.ts`) nor the runtime MCP HTTP path
  (`mcp-http.ts`) provides it

## Root Cause / Fix

Add `authProfileStore?: AuthProfileStore` to `McpLoopbackScopeParams` and thread
it through the full call chain:

```
prepare.ts → ensureMcpLoopbackServer → startMcpLoopbackServer → toolCache.resolve()
                                                              → resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools
                                                                 → resolveGatewayScopedTools
                                                                    → createOpenClawTools(authProfileStore)
```

Both the prepare-time prompt-tools path and the runtime MCP `tools/list` +
`tools/call` path now receive the auth store.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

`startMcpLoopbackServer` started with an xAI OAuth profile in the auth store.
`tools/list` queried via MCP JSON-RPC over HTTP:

target.body:
Closes #101967

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running CLI-backend sessions (e.g., `claude-cli`) with OAuth-only xAI auth would never see the `x_search` and `code_execution` tools on the session tool surface. Because subagents inherit the parent session's tool list, the tools were also stripped from native-runtime Grok subagents spawned from a claude-cli main session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway loopback MCP bridge that feeds CLI-backend sessions resolved plugin tools without passing an `authProfileStore`. Native embedded runs already passed the store, which let the xAI plugin register search/code-execution tools when an OAuth profile was present. This change threads the auth profile store through the same path:

- `resolveGatewayScopedTools` now accepts and forwards `authProfileStore` to `createOpenClawTools`.
- `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` / `McpLoopbackToolCache` accept `authProfileStore`.
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` forwards its already-loaded `authStore` when computing prompt tools.
- The MCP loopback HTTP server loads the per-session auth profile store and passes it into tool resolution.

## User Impact

CLI-backend sessions with OAuth-only xAI auth now correctly surface `x_search` and `code_execution`, and subagents spawned from those sessions inherit the tools as expected.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: emit failover event for successful model fallback chains
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `emitFailoverEvent` was only called from the cooldown/suspend path, so the OTEL `model.failover` diagnostic was never emitted when model fallback actually happened. Multi-hop chains (deepseek-v4-flash → minimax-m2.7 → kimi-k2.6) and all-failed storms were invisible in traces.

**Solution**: Emit a `model.failover` diagnostic event at each failed-candidate → next-candidate transition in the fallback loop. This captures every hop in the chain (from, to, reason, cascade depth) regardless of whether the chain ultimately succeeds or exhausts. The existing `openclaw.failover.*` OTEL attributes already convey fallback occurrence — no undocumented span attribute needed.

**What changed**: `model-fallback.ts`: After recording each failed candidate, emit `model.failover` with `fromProvider/fromModel/toProvider/toModel/reason/cascadeDepth` when a next candidate exists. `diagnostics-otel/service.ts`: Removed new undocumented `has_fallback` attribute (reverted to baseline — existing `openclaw.failover.*` attributes are sufficient).

**What did NOT change**: The cooldown/suspend `emitFailoverEvent` call site. Fallback decision logging. Session suspension. Model candidate resolution.

Fixes #102015

## What Problem This Solves

Model fallback chains happen frequently in production (rate limits, provider outages, model deprecations), but the OTEL `model.failover` diagnostic event was never fired during actual fallback. This prevented operators from detecting retry storms and distinguishing single-model sessions from multi-model cascades.

## Root Cause

`emitFailoverEvent` was only called from one location — the `suspend_lanes` cooldown path. The actual fallback loop (`runWithModelFallbackInternal`) never emitted diagnostics for failed-candidate transitions or successful fallback recoveries.

## Design decision

The emit is placed at the **failed-candidate → next-candidate transition** rather than at success. This covers both all-failed chains (every hop gets a `model.failover` event) and successful chains (the last failed hop before success generates the diagnostic). Success-path emission was removed per review feedback — the transition events already capture the full chain.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `model.failover` diagnostic events fire for each failed-candidate → next-candidate transition in multi-hop fallback chains.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 24.13.1

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
pnpm test -- src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.probe.test.ts extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output
model-fallback.test.ts        115 passed (115)
model-fallback.probe.test.ts   20 passed (20)
OTEL service.test.ts          107 passed (107)
TOTAL                         242 passed (242)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Each failed-candidate transition in the fallback loop emits a `model.failover` diagnostic event carrying `from/to provider/model`, `reason`, and `cascadeDepth`. The existing cooldown/suspend path is unchanged. 242 existing tests pass without modification.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end OTLP exporter validation requiring a configured telemetry receiver.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — only adds diagnostic event emissions, no behavioral change
- [x] All 242 existing tests pass unchanged
- [x] 2 files, net +0 lines (move from success path to transition point)
- [x] Cooldown/suspend `emitFailoverEvent` call site unchanged
- [x] No new span attributes — existing `openclaw.failover.*` attributes used
- [x] No breaking API changes, no new dependencies
